history.heading: Persian heritage
paragraphs: Tajikistan, a mountainous country in Central Asia, was part of ancient Persian-speaking civilisations such as Bactria and Sogdiana, important on the Silk Road. Penjikent was a major Sogdian city. The Tajiks trace their heritage to the Samanid dynasty (9th–10th centuries), a Persian empire centred in Bukhara whose founder, Ismoil Somoni, is the national hero.
The region was later ruled by Turkic and Mongol dynasties and the Emirate of Bukhara. The Russian Empire took control in the late 19th century.

history.heading: Soviet era and civil war
paragraphs: The Tajik SSR was created in 1929, but historic Tajik cultural centres such as Samarkand and Bukhara were left in Uzbekistan. Tajikistan became independent on 9 September 1991.

A civil war from 1992 to 1997 between the government and a coalition of Islamist and democratic opposition groups killed up to 100,000 people. Emomali Rahmon, who came to power in 1992, has ruled since, increasingly concentrating power.

culture.heading: Traditions
paragraphs: Tajik, a variety of Persian written in Cyrillic, is the state language, and Russian is widely used. Most people are Sunni Muslim, with Ismaili Shia communities in the Pamirs. Nowruz is the main celebration. Shashmaqam music is recognised by UNESCO.
Plov (oshi palov) is the national dish, and traditional hospitality is important. The Pamir Mountains, the "Roof of the World", cover much of the country.

politics.heading: Authoritarian rule
paragraphs: Tajikistan is formally a presidential republic, but power is concentrated in President Rahmon and his family; his son Rustam Emomali is speaker of the upper house and widely seen as successor. Opposition parties have been banned and critics imprisoned. Tajikistan hosts a Russian military base and is a CSTO member. A long border dispute with Kyrgyzstan was settled in 2025.

economy.heading: Remittances and hydropower
paragraphs: Tajikistan is the poorest country in Central Asia. Remittances from Tajik migrants working mainly in Russia make up around 40 percent of GDP, among the highest shares in the world. Aluminium (from the TALCO smelter), cotton and gold are exports.
The country has enormous hydropower potential; the Rogun Dam, under construction, would be the world's tallest. The currency is the somoni.
